evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 漢字構形資料庫
evidence.text: Lists oracle-bone forms (two examples), bronze forms (including inscription 集成04178), Chu manuscripts, and small seal. Its account says the bronze/oracle form depicts two 又 (hands) oriented alike, even joined, to indicate friendliness; in small seal, the two 又 shapes were arranged vertically. This supports a semantic “two hands” analysis but does not establish that the depicted cooperation was the historically intended concept.
evidence.title: 漢字「友」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 形義通解; 甲骨、金文用例
evidence.text: Presents both a semantic and phonetic account: the two 同向又 shapes suggest friendliness, and 又 also serves as phonetic. It reports oracle-bone use for a personal name and a reading as 侑 in a sacrificial context; bronze inscriptions use 友 for friend/friendly or associates, citing 趞曹鼎「用卿(饗)朋友」, 牆盤「隹(惟)辟孝友」, and 令方彝「乃寮與乃友」. It also records a loan reading 柔 in the Mawangdui Laozi manuscripts, with甲本「友弱勝強」 corresponding to乙本「柔弱勝強」. The page does not provide absolute dates for these individual witnesses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：友

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: Reports the received Shuowen account: 「同志為友。从二又。相交友也」, glossing 友 as those sharing purposes and describing the graph as two 又. Its definitions and examples include a noun ‘friend’, the verb ‘make friends/be acquainted’ with a Lunyu example, ‘love’, and ‘assist/cooperate’; these are dictionary-organized senses and do not by themselves prove their chronological order.
evidence.title: A00470 友 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: Identifies two 又 components, each glossed as hand and as contributing sound, and gives the character’s reported Old Chinese *[ɢ]ʷəʔ, Middle Chinese hjuwX, and Mandarin yǒu. It labels the earliest displayed oracle forms approximately 1250–1000 BCE and an early Western Zhou bronze form approximately 1000 BCE. Its semantic-pictograph account conflicts in emphasis with the Chinese University of Hong Kong account, which explicitly treats 又 as a phonetic as well as semantic element. The dates are the site's labels for displayed examples, not dates independently established here for every use.
evidence.title: 友 — Dong Chinese

evidence.text: Reports 又 as a pictograph of a hand and identifies ‘again’ as a phonetic loan. It gives 又 Old Chinese *[ɢ]ʷəʔ-s, Middle Chinese hjuwH, Mandarin yòu. This is a separate component reading record from the host 友 reading. Its loan account concerns the development of 又’s own written uses and is distinct from 又’s phonetic role within 友.
evidence.title: 又 — Dong Chinese

evidence.source: Wiktionary Chinese character entry, reporting Zhengzhang Shangfang (2003) and Baxter–Sagart (2014); local Baxter–Sagart table row supplied in input
evidence.text: Reports Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese 又 *ɢʷɯs and 友 *ɢʷɯʔ, as well as Baxter–Sagart (2014) 友 *[ɢ]ʷəʔ. The local Baxter–Sagart table row for 友 confirms the latter notation; the local packet has no 又 row, so no local B–S comparison for that character is asserted. Within Zhengzhang's system, 又 and 友 share the initial and medial/rime material but differ in final *-s versus *-ʔ. This makes a phonetic role plausible; it does not resolve whether both repeated 又 forms are phonetic or whether one/both are also semantic.

evidence.field: 廣韻; early graph uses; graph/sense history
evidence.text: Records the Guangyun fanqie 云久 and Middle Chinese category 云母, rising tone, 尤/有 rhyme, open division III. Separately, it distinguishes early use of the graph: oracle-bone examples are read as a personal name or as 侑 ‘assist in sacrifice’; Western Zhou bronze examples include friend/friendly and associate/official uses. These are graphic uses with their own contexts, not a sequence inferred from a modern gloss list.

gaps: The graph's earliest contexts available here are reported as Shang oracle-bone personal-name and 侑 sacrificial uses; these do not establish ‘friend’ as its earliest attested sense. Individual oracle-bone and bronze witnesses were not independently inspected as primary artifacts, and the dictionary page provides no absolute dates for the cited inscriptions.

The semantic ‘two cooperating hands’ account and the phono-semantic account are not mutually exclusive in all sources: CUHK explicitly gives 又 both semantic and phonetic roles. The exact contribution of each repeated 又 shape remains unresolved; no independent phonetic comparison in the same reconstruction system was verified for 友 and 又 beyond reported Zhengzhang values.

No sound-loan claim for the entire graph 友 is required by the evidence examined. The Mawangdui 友-for-柔 spelling is reported by CUHK, but its underlying reading is a separate lexical loan, not an explanation of graph formation.

The stated semantic extension chain from personal name/侑 to friend, verb ‘befriend’, and ‘friendly’ is not established. The sources attest distinct contextual uses; a continuous chronology or semantic bridge should not be asserted.

Official Unicode Unihan records for U+53CB and U+53C8 were attempted but inaccessible through the web tool. The supplied local kMandarin row supports yǒu for 友; no local row was supplied for 又. An official Unicode click-through citation could not be verified.
No licensed-bulk-reuse terms were verified for the recurring character database material; cite character-specific pages rather than recommending a local extract.
